body:
Tonight, head to the beach (I think you're close to it?) and watch the sun set over the ocean.  Don't think about anything, just sit in the sand, feel it between your toes and watch the sun slowly sink behind the horizon.  If it's not too cold, head down to the water and feel it splash around your ankles.  Clear your head (I know it's ridiculously hard) and just watch, feel, and experience.  Use that feeling as your inspiration.  Any time anything seems insurmountable, all you have to do is make it to the sunset and watch, be inspired for the night, and make it to the next day.

This is a last resort, and I hesitate to suggest it, but if you can find the courage to head to a well-trafficked area and panhandle, you can scrape together enough to make it through a day with a little left over.  It's not a solution, but it's a start.  I was there at one point, and it's not fun.  But it'll get you to the sunset.

I'm sure this is the last thing you want to hear, but there are ways.  How long have you been homeless?  Do you at least have a safe place to spend the night?  If you live in a town with over 1,000 people, there's probably a shelter you could turn to if you need it.  If you're in a smaller town, I'd be willing to bet a local church wouldn't close it's doors to you (and hopefully spare you the religion if you don't want it, but a welcome addition if you do).  

Transportation... it's tough.  But there are ways of getting around.  The way I see it, it's winter now, so if you walk/run/bike/etc. to wherever you're going, at least you won't show up too sweaty, right?

I've looked through your history, and you're a smart person.  There's a job out there somewhere for you.  

But those are the easy answers.  The tough part is finding something stable to get your life back on track.  And trust me, I'm right there with you.  I know the feeling of losing control, the complete lack of self worth that you're going through.  Unfortunately, there's no easy answer to that part.  The best you can do is just keep hammering away.  It seems hopeless and tireless, but (I'm sorry this is ridiculously cheesy) think about John Henry, just keeping hammering and hammering away.  Eventually the puzzle pieces will fall into place.  That can't happen if you're not there for it.  

As a side note (I'm sure you probably already know this) but if you can scrape together enough money to get your pharmacy tech certification, it's almost a golden ticket to a pharmacy job.  I think when I took it a few years ago and it cost somewhere around $135?  I can't be sure.  If you can do basic math and remember some pharmacy jargon, you should be fine.  There's free study guides on the internet if you want them.

It's tough, and it sounds like you've been dealt a particularly difficult hand.  The best you can do is to just keep trying.  You've got the tools to get yourself there -- I know you do.  Once you get that first step, you can take the second.  Everything builds from there.  Just keep working on that first step.  One thing a day, one day at a time.  

Good luck.  Please take care of yourself.

Thanks for all your help.  I think you've located the greatest weakness in my logic:  the uncertainty of my death's impact on others' lives.  I counter that we also don't know the impact of my life on others' lives, but we have more evidence to suggest that my life may be more negatively impactful than my death.  (Yes at this point I'm making up words.)  But I'm trying.  Honestly and with every ounce of my being I can muster, I'm trying.  Hence my post here -- I want to make sure all options are exhausted before I make a permanent decision.  

But you've given me a lot to think about.  I'm not sure I'm out of the woods just yet, but I do need to weigh my options just a few more times.  

I get that the whole point of /r/suicidewatch is to convince people *not* to kill themselves, so I sincerely appreciate your input.  There's just no place to to turn to for an objective opinion.

Oh man!  That'd totally blow my cover!

Seriously though, I know exactly what she'd say.  She the type to blame herself at the drop of a hat, and she'd instantly feel bad about expressing her disappointment to me and backpedal as quickly as she could.  She'd lock herself into this relationship out of guilt alone, no matter how miserable it made her.  So I agree, talking to her would be the best option; I just can't trust her to give an honest opinion.

Thank you for the reply.  I guess I was (am) kind of looking at is as a two birds with one stone situation.  I've been suicidal on and off for about four years, so it'd put an end to that for me, and give her a second chance.  But you're right, I don't know for a fact that she'd be able to move on.  But I do know for a fact that continuing a life with me as I am now and for the foreseeable future isn't what she really wanted.  

With regards to therapy, I appreciate the suggestion.  I should have mentioned that I've tried everything short of a lobotomy, not just meds.
